answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the pearl identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator pays for 393 runs and collects one. Because the tundra index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the nadir audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 393 answers need 393 separate inference runs with separate seeds. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
